title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - D-22
notes:
West leads the ♠6 against 3NT. East wins the spade opening lead with the ♠A and continues with the ♠J. It seems natural for South to cover with the ♠Q, but to do so would jeopardize the contract on the above layout of the East-West spades and clubs.

West will make the fine play of allowing South's ♠Q to win the trick and when East wins the ♣K, the defense will be in a position to win 3 more spade tricks to defeat the contract.

South can (and should) guard against this danger by refusing to cover East's ♠J at trick 2. This unusual refusal to cover allows South to retain his spade stopper while exhausting East (the dangerous opponent) of spades. East will continue spades to West's ♠K (no other suit is better) and West is welcome to clear the suit.

South can now take the club finesse, safe in the knowledge that only East (who cannot hurt South in spades) can win the trick. South can win whatever East returns and, with the clubs established, South has more than enough tricks for the contract.
